concepts.why: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by Hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is highly suggestive of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.
The patient's low hemoglobin level and low platelet count, in combination with the presence of atypical cells, could be indicative of extramedullary hematopoiesis.
The patient's widespread, nontender, erythematous patches and thin plaques, some with prominent overlying telangiectases and hyperpigmentation, could be indicative of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
The patient's history of pembrolizumab treatment and the development of a new widespread skin eruption could be indicative of a pembrolizumab-induced rash.
The patient's low platelet count and the absence of growth on blood culture could be indicative of disseminated intravascular coagulation.
The patient's low white blood cell count, low hemoglobin level, and low platelet count could be indicative of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
The patient's hypotension and the presence of widespread, nontender, erythematous patches and thin plaques could be indicative of systemic vasculitis.
The patient's history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis and the absence of growth on blood culture could be indicative of coccidioidomycosis.
The patient's low white blood cell count, low hemoglobin level, and low platelet count could be indicative of severe aplastic anemia.
The patient's low white blood cell count, low hemoglobin level, and low platelet count could be indicative of a bone marrow failure syndrome.
